Let $h>0$, let $I_i=[ih,(i+1)h)$, let $x_i=(i+\tfrac12)h$ be its center, and write $x_{i+1/2}=(i+1)h$ and $x_{i-1/2}=ih$ for its right and left faces. For real $a,b$, define
$$\operatorname{minmod}(a,b)=\begin{cases}\operatorname{sgn}(a)\min(|a|,|b|),&ab>0,\\0,&ab\le0.\end{cases}$$

At the face $y_{i+1/2}=(i+\tfrac12)h$, set $d_L=|[y_{i-1},y_i,y_{i+1}]V|$ and $d_R=|[y_i,y_{i+1},y_{i+2}]V|$. Choose the left triple when $d_L\le d_R$ and otherwise choose the right triple. For the selected triple $(y_a,y_b,y_c)$ define its Newton quadratic by
$$P_{a,b,c}(y)=V_a+\frac{V_b-V_a}{y_b-y_a}(y-y_a)+[y_a,y_b,y_c]V\,(y-y_a)(y-y_b).$$

$$\operatorname{minmod}(a,b)=\begin{cases}\operatorname{sgn}(a)\min(|a|,|b|),&ab>0,\\0,&ab\le0.\end{cases}$$
The **MUSCL/minmod reconstruction** assigns the cell slope $s_i=h^{-1}\operatorname{minmod}(U_i-U_{i-1},U_{i+1}-U_i)$ and the two face states $U_{i-1/2}^{+,M}=U_i-hs_i/2$ and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,M}=U_i+hs_i/2$. Here $+$ denotes a trace from the right cell and $-$ a trace from the left cell.

For separate **nodal** data $V_j=u(y_j)$ at $y_j=jh$, define the second divided difference by $[y_a,y_b,y_c]V=(((V_c-V_b)/(y_c-y_b))-((V_b-V_a)/(y_b-y_a)))/(y_c-y_a)$. At the face $y_{i+1/2}=(i+\tfrac12)h$, set $d_L=|[y_{i-1},y_i,y_{i+1}]V|$ and $d_R=|[y_i,y_{i+1},y_{i+2}]V|$. Choose the left triple when $d_L\le d_R$ and otherwise choose the right triple. For the selected triple $(y_a,y_b,y_c)$ define its Newton quadratic by
$$P_{a,b,c}(y)=V_a+\frac{V_b-V_a}{y_b-y_a}(y-y_a)+[y_a,y_b,y_c]V\,(y-y_a)(y-y_b).$$
The **nodal ENO2 face value** is $P_{a,b,c}(y_{i+1/2})$. This nodal interpolation branch is distinct from the cell-average WENO branch below.

For cell averages $U_{i-2},\ldots,U_{i+2}$, define the left-biased WENO5 candidate face functionals
$$p_0=(2U_{i-2}-7U_{i-1}+11U_i)/6,\qquad p_1=(-U_{i-1}+5U_i+2U_{i+1})/6,\qquad p_2=(2U_i+5U_{i+1}-U_{i+2})/6.$$
Define the Jiang–Shu indicators
$$\beta_0=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_{i-2}-2U_{i-1}+U_i)^2+\tfrac14(U_{i-2}-4U_{i-1}+3U_i)^2,$$
$$\beta_1=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_{i-1}-2U_i+U_{i+1})^2+\tfrac14(U_{i-1}-U_{i+1})^2,\qquad \beta_2=\tfrac{13}{12}(U_i-2U_{i+1}+U_{i+2})^2+\tfrac14(3U_i-4U_{i+1}+U_{i+2})^2.$$
Fix a positive parameter $\epsilon_0$ with the same units as each $\beta_k$, independently of $h$, and ideal weights $(d_0,d_1,d_2)=(1/10,6/10,3/10)$. If $u$ is nondimensionalized, $\epsilon_0$ is a fixed positive number. The **WENO-JS weights** and left face value are $\alpha_k^J=d_k/(\epsilon_0+\beta_k)^2$, $\omega_k^J=\alpha_k^J/\sum_{l=0}^2\alpha_l^J$, and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,J}=\sum_{k=0}^2\omega_k^Jp_k$. The **WENO-Z comparison weights** use $\tau_5=|\beta_0-\beta_2|$, $\alpha_k^Z=d_k[1+(\tau_5/(\epsilon_0+\beta_k))^2]$, $\omega_k^Z=\alpha_k^Z/\sum_{l=0}^2\alpha_l^Z$, and $U_{i+1/2}^{-,Z}=\sum_{k=0}^2\omega_k^Zp_k$. All denominators are positive because $\epsilon_0>0$ and every $\beta_k$ is a sum of squares. The right face state is obtained by reflection about that face: replace each stencil value $U_k$ in the displayed left formula by $U_{2i+1-k}$.

For scalar linear advection $u_t+a u_x=0$, a **direct reconstructed-upwind forward-Euler update** uses $\nu=a\Delta t/h$, the flux $F_{i+1/2}=aU_{i+1/2}^{-,M}$ when $a\ge0$ and $F_{i+1/2}=aU_{i+1/2}^{+,M}$ when $a<0$, and $U_i^{n+1}=U_i^n-(\Delta t/h)(F_{i+1/2}-F_{i-1/2})$. The total variation of a sequence is $\operatorname{TV}(U)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}|U_{i+1}-U_i|$ when the sum is finite; **TVD** means that this quantity does not increase in one update.

For a vector system whose flux Jacobian at an interface is diagonalizable as $A=R\Lambda R^{-1}$ with real diagonal $\Lambda$, a **characteristic-wise reconstruction** applies a chosen scalar reconstruction to the components of $R^{-1}U$ and maps the reconstructed vector back by $R$. This definition alone gives no TVD or stability result for systems.

derivations.claim:
First suppose $a>0$. If $d_i\ne0$, then $m_i/d_i$ and $m_{i-1}/d_i$ lie in $[0,1]$: in each minmod, $d_i$ is one argument, so a nonzero output has the sign of $d_i$ and magnitude at most $|d_i|$. Set
$$C_i=\mu\left[1+\frac{m_i/d_i-m_{i-1}/d_i}{2}\right]$$
in this case. If $d_i=0$, then $m_i=m_{i-1}=0$; set $C_i=\mu$. In either case $\mu/2\le C_i\le3\mu/2$, and the exact update satisfies $U_i^+=U_i-C_id_i=(1-C_i)U_i+C_iU_{i-1}$. Thus $0\le C_i\le1$ when $\mu\le2/3$, including equality.

Subtract the identity for $U_{i-1}^+$ in step 1.1 from that for $U_i^+$ to obtain $d_i^+=(1-C_i)d_i+C_{i-1}d_{i-1}$. The coefficients are nonnegative, so $|d_i^+|\le(1-C_i)|d_i|+C_{i-1}|d_{i-1}|$. For periodic data, $C_i$ is $N$-periodic because it is defined from shifts of $U$; summing over one period and cyclically reindexing gives $\operatorname{TV}_N(U^+)\le\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}[(1-C_i)+C_i]|d_i|=\operatorname{TV}_N(U)$. This also covers $N=1$, when every $d_i=0$. For bi-infinite data, both nonnegative series on the right are bounded by $\sum_i|d_i|<\infty$. Reindexing the absolutely convergent second series gives $\operatorname{TV}(U^+)\le\sum_i[(1-C_i)+C_i]|d_i|=\operatorname{TV}(U)$, so the updated sequence still has finite variation.

Now suppose $a<0$. At face $i+1/2$, [F2] gives $F_{i+1/2}=a(U_{i+1}-m_{i+1}/2)$ and $F_{i-1/2}=a(U_i-m_i/2)$, hence $U_i^+=U_i+\mu[(U_{i+1}-U_i)-(m_{i+1}-m_i)/2]$. Reflect the data by $V_j=U_{-j}$. Its minmod increments obey $m_j^V=-m_{-j}$, because reflection reverses each adjacent difference and minmod is odd under simultaneous sign reversal. With $i=-j$, the positive-speed expression for $V_j$ is $V_j-\mu[(V_j-V_{j-1})+(m_j^V-m_{j-1}^V)/2]=U_i+\mu[(U_{i+1}-U_i)-(m_{i+1}-m_i)/2]$, exactly the negative-speed update just computed. Also $V_j-V_{j-1}=-(U_{-j+1}-U_{-j})$, so reflection only reindexes the absolute increments and preserves both the bi-infinite and periodic variation sums. Step 2.1 therefore proves the claim for negative velocity. If $a=0$, both fluxes vanish; if $\Delta t=0$, their difference is multiplied by zero in the update. In either case the update is the identity, covering $\mu=0$.

Fix $2/3<\mu\le1$, any $h>0$ and any $a\ne0$, and take $\Delta t=\mu h/|a|$. For positive velocity choose $U_{-1}=U_1=1/2$, $U_0=1$, and $U_i=0$ otherwise; its initial variation is $|1/2|+|1/2|+|{-1/2}|+|{-1/2}|=2$. The only nonzero differences are $d_{-1}=d_0=1/2$ and $d_1=d_2=-1/2$, so the only nonzero minmod increments are $m_{-1}=1/2$ and $m_1=-1/2$. Substituting these in [F2], the four affected updates are $U_{-1}^+=1/2-\mu(1/2+1/4)=A$, $U_0^+=1-\mu(1/2-1/4)=B$, $U_1^+=1/2-\mu(-1/2-1/4)=C$, and $U_2^+=0-\mu(-1/2+1/4)=D$, where $A=1/2-3\mu/4$, $B=1-\mu/4$, $C=1/2+3\mu/4$, and $D=\mu/4$; every other update is zero because its state and all adjacent minmod increments are zero. Here $A<0$, $B\ge3/4>0$, $C-B=\mu-1/2>0$, $D>0$, and $C-D=1/2+\mu/2>0$, so $A<0<B<C$ and $0<D<C$. Hence $\operatorname{TV}(U^+)= -A+(B-A)+(C-B)+(C-D)+D=2(C-A)=3\mu>2$. For negative velocity reflect this witness; step 3.1 preserves its updated variation. Periodizing the data with any $N\ge7$ leaves at least four zero initial cells between successive three-cell supports and at least three zero updated entries between the four affected entries; since a positive-velocity update uses only cells $i-2,\ldots,i+1$ and a negative-velocity update uses only cells $i-1,\ldots,i+2$, no stencil meets two distinct support copies, and the periodic variation is the same $3\mu$. At $\mu=2/3$, the coefficient argument in steps 1.1–2.1 still proves TVD, and the witness updates to $(0,5/6,1,1/6)$ with variation $2$; every larger CFL number through one fails.

finite_checks.claim: For every 2/3<mu<=1, the finite tent refutes TVD for the direct MUSCL/minmod forward-Euler update.
finite_checks.calculation: Initial variation is 2. The nonzero slopes are m_-1=1/2 and m_1=-1/2. Updated states at -1,0,1,2 are A=1/2-3mu/4, B=1-mu/4, C=1/2+3mu/4, D=mu/4; the ordering A<0<B<C and 0<D<C yields variation 2(C-A)=3mu.

thm-na-musc-minmod-forward-euler-tvd-und.axiom_note: No axiom of choice or dependent-choice principle is used; all arguments and witnesses are explicit and countable summation uses only absolute convergence.
